A.explanation: This is mass multiplied by $g$ per unit volume, so $\text{N m}^{-3}$ is weight density, not mass density.

B.explanation: This is mass divided by length, $\text{g mm}^{-1}$, so it has base units of $\text{kg m}^{-1}$ and cannot be density.

C.explanation: This is mass divided by area, $\text{kg cm}^{-2}$, so it has base units of $\text{kg m}^{-2}$ and cannot be density.

D.explanation: This is mass divided by volume, $\mu\text{g mm}^{-3}$, which has base units of $\text{kg m}^{-3}$ and is a valid unit for density.

hints: Start from the definition of density as mass divided by volume, $\rho = m/V$, so you need a mass unit over a length-cubed unit.
Compare the power of length in each option: $\text{m}^{-3}$ and $\text{mm}^{-3}$ mean per unit volume, while $\text{mm}^{-1}$ and $\text{cm}^{-2}$ mean per unit length and per unit area.
Check whether the numerator is a mass unit or a force unit: $\text{N}$ contains $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, whereas $\text{g}$, $\text{kg}$ and $\mu\text{g}$ are all masses.
walkthrough: Recall the defining equation for density: $\rho = m/V$, where $m$ is mass and $V$ is volume.
Therefore any unit for density must be of the form $\text{mass unit divided by volume unit}$, with SI base form $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
Option A uses $\text{N}$, and since $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$ it is a unit of force, so $\text{N m}^{-3}$ is weight per unit volume, not density.
Options B and C fail on the denominator power: $\text{g mm}^{-1}$ is mass per length and $\text{kg cm}^{-2}$ is mass per area, neither is mass per $\text{length}^{3}$.
Option D has numerator $\mu\text{g}$, a mass, and denominator $\text{mm}^{3}$, a volume, so $\mu\text{g mm}^{-3}$ simplifies to mass per volume with correct power $-3$.
